text:
Customer - AcmeApp: hitting a weird one — when our users stream completions we sometimes get a partial response, then the client reconnects and we see duplicate tokens billed. Happens intermittently (~1-2% of streams). Repro steps below. No customer-visible 500s, just partial content.
Alice (Support): thanks — can you share a minimal repro and any client logs? Do you see a 401 or 403 right before the reconnect?
Customer - AcmeApp: attaching logs — we do see a short auth failure in some runs. Example: 
```
[stream] got chunk: "Hello, wor"
[stream] connection closed: EOF
[auth] refresh started
[auth] refresh ok
[stream] reconnect -> new SSE connection
[stream] got chunk: "ld!"
```
Billing shows tokens from both fragments as full billing (we get charged twice).
Ben (SDK): hm sounds like our client is automatically replaying pending buffer when it reconnects. We changed the iterator resume logic in 2.1.3 to try to be helpful. Could be a race where auth refresh triggers a new request and we resend already-delivered chunks. Which SDK + version?
Customer - AcmeApp: using python sdk 2.1.3 (async iterator).
Alice (Support): Ben, can you weigh in on the async iterator resume semantics? If the client resends previously received bytes that could double-bill.
Ben (SDK): yep — probable regression. The async iterator keeps an internal buffer (pending_events) and on reconnect it drains pending_events into the new stream. There was a change to call drain() during auth refresh which can double-send if the previous connection delivered the chunks but client didn't mark them acknowledged due to EOF.
Carol (SRE): seeing similar traces in prod — here's a compiled sequence I pulled from our edge logs: 
```
edge  - stream open id=abc123
edge  - auth 401 id=abc123
client - starts refresh
edge  - stream close id=abc123 reason=EOF
client - reconnect id=abc123 new_conn
client - initial payload includes: <resend_marker> + pending chunks
edge  - accepts chunks -> bills tokens
```
This matches the partial/duplicate billing pattern.
Alice (Support): ok can you provide a small repro snippet we can run locally? Even pseudo code is fine.
Customer - AcmeApp: here's the flow we used in python: 
```python
# pseudo
async def stream():
    async for chunk in client.chat.stream(...):
        print(chunk.text)
        if some_network_glitch: break # triggers EOF
    # client auto-refreshes token and reconnects
```
We can reproduce by pausing the server right after sending first chunks then resuming.
Ben (SDK): repro confirmed locally with simulated auth expiry. Root cause: when connection ends with EOF instead of explicit final event, the iterator didn't mark delivered chunks as acked; then on reconnect drain() duplicates them into the new request. I have a failing unit test.
Alice (Support): mitigation for customers while we patch?
Ben (SDK): short term: pin to 2.1.2 (no auto-drain on reconnect), or set environment var REDWOOD_SDK_STREAM_ACK=true which will enable explicit acking (internal toggle) — that prevents replay. We'll make a proper fix in 2.1.4.
Carol (SRE): I'll add a temporary server-side detector to ignore immediate replays within 500ms of EOF from same client id — reduces duplicate billing noise while SDK patch lands.
Customer - AcmeApp: appreciate it. What's the timeline?
Ben (SDK): PR up, fix in code + unit tests. Plan to cut patch 2.1.4 tomorrow EOD, release early next week. I'll add migration notes about auth-refresh and the race.
Alice (Support): created internal ticket RW-STREAM-2026 and linked customer. Will update SLA thread.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: canary -> us-west-2 (edge replay detector).
Carol (SRE): monitoring alert rule added: duplicate-billing-rate > 0.5% -> paging.
Alice (Support): closing loop — temporary workaround for you: pin to 2.1.2 or set REDWOOD_SDK_STREAM_ACK=true; we'll follow up once 2.1.4 is released. Thanks for the detailed repro and logs :thumbsup:
Customer - AcmeApp: thanks all — will try the env var and report back.
